result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.ada_star_search()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find path using ADA* (Anytime Dynamic A*) search algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17616-L17813){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.ada_star_search( source, target, epsilon=1.0, weight_attr="weight", heuristic=None, reuse_planner=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ADA* is an anytime optimal pathfinding algorithm that can return suboptimal paths quickly and iteratively improve them. The epsilon parameter controls the trade-off between solution quality and speed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting node ID or label. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node ID or label. [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Suboptimality bound. epsilon=1.0 finds optimal paths, epsilon>1.0 trades optimality for speed. Higher values explore less but may return longer paths. [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["weight"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute to use as weight. Falls back to `edge.weight` if attribute not found. [heuristic]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable[[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]], float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Custom heuristic function `h(node, target) -> float` that estimates cost from any node to target. Parameters can be node IDs (int) or labels (str). Must be admissible (never overestimate). If `None`, uses zero heuristic (equivalent to Dijkstra's algorithm). [reuse_planner]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, reuses planner state from previous call with same source/target. Enables iterative refinement by calling with decreasing epsilon values. If `False`, creates fresh planner for each call. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Path from source to target as list of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target nodes don't exist, or if no path exists. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(b^d)` where `b` is the branching factor, `d` is depth - space complexity: `O(b^d)` for storing search states - `epsilon=1.0` guarantees optimal paths (A* behavior) - `epsilon>1.0` provides bounded suboptimality with faster search - the algorithm performs backward search from target to source - set `reuse_planner=True` for iterative refinement with decreasing epsilon - planner state is stored in `graph._ada_star_planner` attribute - different source/target pairs automatically create separate planners ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find optimal path (equivalent to Dijkstra): ::: {#47f830e4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B", attributes={"weight": 1.0}) .add_edge("A", "C", attributes={"weight": 4.0}) .add_edge("B", "C", attributes={"weight": 2.0}) .add_edge("C", "D", attributes={"weight": 1.0}) .add_edge("B", "D", attributes={"weight": 5.0}) ) graph.ada_star_search("A", "D", epsilon=1.0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 4] ``` ::: ::: Raising `epsilon=` explores less of the graph and returns faster, at the cost of potentially settling for a longer path: ::: {#4fc2e08f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="C", weight=4.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="D", weight=5.0) ) graph.ada_star_search(source="A", target="D", epsilon=5.0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: ::: Custom heuristic (e.g., Euclidean distance for spatial graphs): ::: {#727c4aa5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="A", x=0.0, y=0.0) .add_node(label="B", x=1.0, y=0.0) .add_node(label="C", x=1.0, y=1.0) .add_node(label="D", x=2.0, y=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="C", weight=4.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="D", weight=5.0) ) # Heuristic using labels def euclidean_labels(node: str, target: str) -> float: n1 = graph.get_node_from_label(node) n2 = graph.get_node_from_label(target) x1, y1 = n1.attributes["x"], n1.attributes["y"] x2, y2 = n2.attributes["x"], n2.attributes["y"] return ((x2 - x1)**2 + (y2 - y1)**2)**0.5 graph.ada_star_search(source="A", target="D", heuristic=euclidean_labels) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: ::: The heuristic can just as easily work with node IDs instead of labels: ::: {#d8769933 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def euclidean_ids(node_id: int, target_id: int) -> float: n1 = graph.get_node(node_id) n2 = graph.get_node(target_id) x1, y1 = n1.attributes["x"], n1.attributes["y"] x2, y2 = n2.attributes["x"], n2.attributes["y"] return ((x2 - x1)**2 + (y2 - y1)**2)**0.5 a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") graph.ada_star_search(source=a_id, target=d_id, heuristic=euclidean_ids) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: ::: With `reuse_planner=True`, successive calls with decreasing epsilon refine the same search instead of starting over, letting you get a quick answer first and improve it later: ::: {#0e802672 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="C", weight=4.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=2.0) .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="B", target="D", weight=5.0) ) # Quick suboptimal path first graph.ada_star_search(source="A", target="D", epsilon=5.0, reuse_planner=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3ca0cc1b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Refine to a better path (reuses previous work) graph.ada_star_search(source="A", target="D", epsilon=2.0, reuse_planner=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#071ffef3 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Get the optimal path (reuses previous work again) graph.ada_star_search(source="A", target="D", epsilon=1.0, reuse_planner=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` [1, 2, 3, 4] ``` ::: :::
